target.name: EU Digital Identity Wallet Architecture and Reference Framework

method.claimBoundary: Readiness mapping only. No EUDI compliance, certification, formal audit or GAAM conformance claim is made.

findings.title: Action-level authority is not uniformly represented
findings.observation: Authority is often derived from role, registration, certification, trusted-list state and protocol rules rather than one common action-level representation.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Model authority as a resolvable tuple of source, actor, action, subject or resource, scope, constraints, validity and revocation state where consequential effects depend on authority.
candidateTests: reject valid identity without action authority
reject authority outside declared scope
accept authority only while source and status remain valid

enforcement: role, registration, certification and protocol checks

establishes: recognition or status facts within source scope

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Role authority is distributed across governance sources
findings.observation: Role definitions and their operative authority can depend on legislation, implementing acts, ARF requirements, certification and national arrangements.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Publish a role-to-authority register that resolves each governed role to authority sources, permitted effects, constraints and lifecycle conditions.
candidateTests: resolve every consequential role to at least one authority source
detect conflicting or missing role-authority mappings

establishes: role identity and applicable governance sources
doesNotEstablish: uniform authority independent of jurisdiction or rule source

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Authority conflict and precedence require explicit treatment
findings.observation: Several legitimate legal, supervisory, certification and technical authority sources can apply simultaneously.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Represent precedence, coordination, refusal and escalation rules for overlapping authority sources as explicit governance data.
candidateTests: resolve two applicable authorities with conflicting outcomes
fail closed when precedence is undefined

revocation: supersession or withdrawal of authority source

doesNotEstablish: deterministic precedence when no rule is declared

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Runtime governance decisions lack a common decision envelope
findings.observation: Protocol validation is substantial, but no general envelope consistently records the authority, rule, evidence, constraints and decision behind a consequential effect.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Define a privacy-minimised runtime governance envelope for consequential decisions, preserving resolvable evidence references instead of unnecessary transaction data.
candidateTests: decision cannot be reconstructed when required evidence is absent
stale evidence triggers configured denial, restriction or review

doesNotEstablish: privacy-safe accountability if excessive transaction data is logged

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Decision receipts are not systemic
findings.observation: There is no general privacy-preserving receipt connecting a material effect to the authority and evidence supporting the decision.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Prototype bounded decision receipts that expose accountability evidence without creating a cross-context correlation layer.
candidateTests: receipt supports independent reconstruction of the declared decision basis
receipt omits prohibited or unnecessary correlating data

doesNotEstablish: permission to create cross-context surveillance or correlation

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Revocation dependency propagation is uneven
findings.observation: Status and revocation mechanisms exist, but downstream consequences of changing an upstream governance artifact are not represented through one dependency model.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Represent authority dependencies explicitly and attach propagation semantics to suspension, expiry, revocation and replacement events.
candidateTests: parent revocation invalidates only declared descendants
unaffected branches remain valid
stale descendant state is detected

doesNotEstablish: identical descendant consequences for every event type

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Registry relationship semantics need stronger typing
findings.observation: Trusted Lists, LoTEs, relying-party registers and related directories can encode different forms of registration, recognition, certification and reliance.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Publish machine-readable registry semantics that state what inclusion establishes, what it does not establish, accepted purposes, assurance thresholds and withdrawal conditions.
candidateTests: registry inclusion does not imply universal trust
unrecognised relationship types cannot satisfy authority checks

establishes: the relationship type declared by the registry

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Assurance mechanisms need explicit composition rules
findings.observation: Certification, functional conformance, security and interoperability assurance establish different claims but do not form one explicit composition model.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Define each assurance form's positive scope, limitations, dependencies and allowed composition so assurance cannot silently broaden across domains.
candidateTests: functional conformance cannot satisfy unrelated security assurance
composed claim fails when a required assurance dependency expires

revocation: expiry or loss of required assurance

doesNotEstablish: automatic transfer of assurance from X to unrelated Y

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Continuous assurance is not yet continuous governance assurance
findings.observation: Lifecycle, supervision and continuing obligations exist, but changing authority relationships and assurance blind spots are not uniformly exposed as governance state.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Define monitored governance controls, evidence freshness, drift conditions, blind spots, escalation and suspension semantics.
candidateTests: assurance state degrades when evidence becomes stale
known monitoring gaps are surfaced rather than treated as pass

doesNotEstablish: continuous assurance of the whole governance system by default

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Multi-party accountability is difficult to reconstruct end to end
findings.observation: A consequential wallet interaction may depend on evidence and decisions from several providers, issuers, relying parties, Member States and assurance actors.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Define an accountability lineage that attributes each governed decision and evidence contribution without collapsing responsibilities into a generic ecosystem actor.
candidateTests: reconstruct accountable parties for a failed decision
delegation does not erase accountability established elsewhere

establishes: individual contributions and responsibilities when evidence exists
doesNotEstablish: single-actor accountability for every ecosystem effect

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Challenge and remedy are not represented as one technical lifecycle
findings.observation: Legal and institutional remedies exist, but a common decision-to-challenge-to-correction-to-remedy lifecycle is not evident across the technical architecture.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Bind material decisions to challenge channels, review authority, correction state and downstream remedy evidence where the framework governs those effects.
candidateTests: materially wrong assurance result is challengeable
correction propagates to affected decision state

doesNotEstablish: one common end-to-end technical remedy lifecycle

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Systemic harm and exclusion observability is limited
findings.observation: Conformance and component assurance do not by themselves demonstrate that combined operation avoids exclusionary or harmful systemic outcomes.
findings.actionableTakeaway: For high-impact deployments, define measurable effect classes, affected-party indicators and escalation thresholds in addition to component correctness.
candidateTests: detect threshold breach in rejection or exclusion indicators
high-impact review is triggered by defined systemic condition

revocation: mitigation or suspension after threshold breach

doesNotEstablish: absence of harmful or exclusionary systemic outcomes

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

findings.title: Machine-readable technical artifacts do not yet form a machine-actionable governance package
findings.observation: The architecture contains substantial machine-readable infrastructure, but authority, registry semantics, assurance scope and remedy are not published as one interoperable governance package.
findings.actionableTakeaway: Prototype an implementation package containing authority, governance-source, registry-semantics, assurance and dependency registers plus runtime and remedy evidence profiles.
candidateTests: package resolves every declared authority and assurance dependency
unknown governance artifacts fail validation

enforcement: authority, registry, assurance and dependency registers

doesNotEstablish: a single interoperable machine-actionable governance chain

knownLimitations: This finding is derived from a governance-framework readiness review, not observed implementation behaviour.
The mapped status does not establish GAAM conformance.

limitations: This mapping is an informative GAAM application exercise and not an official EUDI assessment.
The mapping is based on the assessed ARF version and implementation-oriented source material available at the assessment date.
A status of covered or partial is not a GAAM conformance result and does not establish implementation behaviour.
